title: Research - Panel Matching: explainable scores, a different ranking for every paper
story: Second of the six research cases of one demo slot ({case:research_title} before it, {case:defense-scheduling} after it). Miguel Yu's Form 1 and concept papers have been verified and endorsed. Panel Matching now reads the body text of the three concept papers and compares it with what the Graduate School has recorded about each faculty member: research interests, publications, past advisee and panel titles, degrees and the profile specialization. The research title and the file names are shown for reference but are left out of the comparison.

The point for the panel: the recommendation is explained, not a black box. Every candidate gets a score out of 100 made of three visible parts (expertise 60 points, availability 25, workload 15), the screen names the method used, shows the topics in common, and the student's adviser (Dr. Celeste Tan) is excluded from the panel. To show that the ranking follows the paper, the same screen is then opened for the seven demo papers GS-2026-PM-01 to PM-07, which belong to different fields, and each one produces a different top of the list.
accounts: Opens 6 · Panel Matching, reviews the ranking, selects the panel and finalizes it; opens the Faculty page
data: Miguel Yu, 2260004, MAED (key research-miguel); the Title Defense package comes from the previous case
GS-2026-PM-01 Camille Dizon (MSN), PM-02 Rafael Ocampo (MAPSY), PM-03 Jasper Lorenzo (MSCS), PM-04 Bea Fontanilla (MBA), PM-05 Miko Almario (MBA), PM-06 Liza Marquez (DBA), PM-07 Nico Baltazar (MBA)
Content Specialist: the suggested Dr. Marlon Geronimo (#2) replaced by Dr. Patricia Salvador (#3); Chair Dr. Liwayway Bautista (#1) and Method Specialist Dr. Teodoro Ramos (#6) stay as suggested
For Dr. Teresa Lim, kind Research interest: "Trust, perceived risk, and adoption of digital wallets among young working adults" (added to show the score react, then removed again)

parts.title: Part A - Miguel Yu: how the ranking is built

steps.text: Open **6 · Panel Matching**, search for **2260004** and select **Miguel Yu**. Confirm that the page title is **Panel Matching** and that the selected student reads 2260004 - Yu, Miguel - MAED. Note the bar **Rules applied on this screen** (11 rules from the Graduate School policies, 2 need review).

shots.caption: Panel Matching for Miguel Yu: selected student and the start of the recommendation workspace.

steps.text: Read the green box under **Panel recommendation workspace**: "Three concept papers content ready", 3 of 3 PDFs uploaded and 3 of 3 successfully read, with the note that research titles and file names are excluded. Confirm the badge **Similarity match (keyword TF-IDF)** and the line "Paper analysis: Keyword analysis (local, no AI service)". Read the keywords taken from the papers (for example learning analytics, student engagement, learning management system) and the three paper cards: each lists the file name, the badge **Text extracted**, the analyzed keywords and an excerpt, so staff can see exactly what the system read. The research title is printed as display only.

shots.caption: What the system read: method, keywords and the three paper cards.

steps.text: Scroll to the three boxes: **60 pts** Expertise match (paper vs. faculty records), **25 pts** Availability (conflict-free windows), **15 pts** Workload (other student panels). Then read the sentence that the thesis panel needs 3 members (Panel Chair, Content Specialist, Method Specialist) and the red note **Not eligible for this student's panel**: Dr. Celeste Tan, adviser of this student, cannot sit on the student's panel.

shots.caption: The three weights, the panel size and the adviser who is not eligible.

steps.text: Scroll to the table of ranked panel candidates (the screen shows the top 11 candidates; the boxes **Search faculty**, **Specialization**, **Department / program** and **Availability** above it filter the list). Read the first rows: rank 1 **Dr. Liwayway Bautista** 95.9/100 (expertise 60/60, availability 23.4/25, workload 12.5/15; 5 conflict-free windows, 1 other student panel), rank 2 **Dr. Marlon Geronimo** 67.9/100 (37.6/60, 20.3/25, 10/15), rank 3 **Dr. Patricia Salvador** 52.1/100, rank 4 Dr. Daniel Uy 46.6/100, rank 6 **Dr. Teodoro Ramos** 37.2/100 (23.1/60, 14.1/25, 0/15) with the amber flag **Overloaded** (7 other student panels). The topic chips in each row (for example feedback, learning analytics, online courses for Dr. Bautista) are the terms the paper and the faculty records share. The green rows with the tag **Suggested** are the suggested panel: Chair Bautista, Content Specialist Geronimo, Method Specialist Ramos.

shots.caption: Ranked panel candidates with topics in common, availability, workload and the score bar.

steps.text: Click **Why this score** on rank 1. Read **How the score was built** (Expertise 60 / 60, Availability 23.4 / 25, Workload 12.5 / 15, Total 95.9 / 100), the sentence on how expertise is scaled across the candidate pool, and the line "Method: Similarity match (keyword TF-IDF) (similarity 0.4869)". Read **Passage of the paper that matched** and **Expertise records used**: research interests and a publication, each with the words that matched and the tag **Demo data**. Click **Hide why** again.

shots.caption: Why this score: the three parts, the matched passage and the faculty records used.

parts.title: Part B - Select the panel and finalize

steps.text: Scroll to **Review and adjust the panel set**. The suggested panel is preselected in the three seat lists: **Panel Chair** #1 Dr. Liwayway Bautista - 95.9/100, **Content Specialist** #2 Dr. Marlon Geronimo, **Method Specialist** #6 Dr. Teodoro Ramos - 37.2/100. Under **Panel composition rules** every check shows a tick: all 3 seats filled, every role seated once, a different faculty member in every seat, the adviser not on the panel, Dr. Bautista chairs the panel (University-affiliated faculty), no External Panel seat for a thesis, and Dr. Ramos has recorded research-methods expertise. The badge reads **Staff review**.

shots.caption: The suggested panel preselected, with the panel composition rules.

steps.text: To show that staff decide, open the **Content Specialist** list and choose **#3 Dr. Patricia Salvador - 52.1/100** instead of Dr. Geronimo. Keep Dr. Bautista as **Panel Chair** (this is how the chair is appointed: the seat named Panel Chair).

shots.caption: Content Specialist changed to the #3 candidate.

steps.text: Click **Finalize selected panel**. Confirm that the badge above the seats changes to **Final panel selected** and that the button now reads **Update final panel**.

shots.caption: Final panel selected; the button now reads Update final panel.

steps.text: Open **5 · Research Gate**, search for Miguel Yu and scroll to the card **Panel Matching**. It now shows the badge **Final panel selected** with the three names (Dr. Liwayway Bautista, Dr. Patricia Salvador, Dr. Teodoro Ramos) instead of "Recommended panel available". Each panelist then answers the invitation in the Faculty Portal under Panel Invitations (click Accept; this run accepted all three before the next case). The chair's seat is the one that later records the verdict. Defense Scheduling is the next case ({case:defense-scheduling}).

shots.caption: Research Gate shows the final panel.

parts.title: Part D - Faculty expertise records (the data behind the scores)

steps.text: Before changing anything, select **GS-2026-PM-04** in Panel Matching again and read the row of **Dr. Teresa Lim**: rank 6, score 30/100, expertise 5.9/60.

shots.caption: PM-04 before the edit: Dr. Lim is far down the list.

shots.caption: Dr. Lim's expertise records.

The record added; the message says Panel Matching uses it immediately.

steps.text: Return to Panel Matching, select **GS-2026-PM-04** and read **Dr. Teresa Lim** again: she has moved from rank 6 to rank 3, score 35.6/100, expertise 11.5/60 (it was 5.9). The other scores move slightly because expertise is scaled across the pool (Dr. Santos 40.0 becomes 39.9).

notes: Score = expertise similarity (60) + availability (25) + workload (15). Availability counts conflict-free defense windows (more windows earn more points, up to 25). Workload counts other student panels (fewer panels earn more points); a faculty member with many other panels carries the amber flag Overloaded.

The method label on every screen in this run is Similarity match (keyword TF-IDF), computed locally with no AI service. When an embeddings key is configured the same screen shows Semantic match (Gemini embeddings) instead; that was not enabled in this run (no key) and is not shown here.
The faculty expertise records are demonstration data written for the capstone (tag Demo data), not real USLS faculty records. The stakeholder's real records are still to be provided.

Candidates who share no topic with the paper are listed after those who do, even if their availability or workload points are higher; that is why a lower-scoring faculty member can rank above a higher-scoring one.

The suggested seats are a recommendation only; staff may change any seat. The protocol checks (adviser not on the panel, all seats filled, chair from the University faculty) are repeated on the server when the panel is finalized. The research-methods expertise check for the Method Specialist is advisory.
The panelists answer a panel invitation in their own Faculty Portal (Panel Invitations); a declined seat creates a task for the Research Coordinator to replace the panelist.

The Panel Matching page is wide. The screenshots of this case were taken with a wider window (1700 px) so that all four columns of the table show at once; on a 1366 px screen the table scrolls sideways inside its card.
